translations.translatedText: # Sunday 8.1.2022 (radio)
Guards' actions. Loneliness. Sälen security meeting. Eating vegetables. Weather forecast.
## Guards' actions in a shopping centre
![People in the corridor of Iso Omena.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5015,h_2820,x_456,y_464/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-105677863babeca5578d/1673964182)
Open image viewer
Police suspect that the woman's death may be due to the actions of the guards. Photo: Jouni Immonen / Yle
Police are investigating the actions of the guards of a shopping centre in Espoo. On Saturday a woman died at the Iso Omena shopping centre, whom the guards had apprehended.
Police said on Sunday afternoon that they suspect the guards of manslaughter.
Many people have said that the guards kept the woman on the ground for a long time. The woman became lifeless and attempts were made to resuscitate her, but she died.
## Loneliness
![A woman sits on the ice of a lake.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_6000,h_3375,x_0,y_272/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-775224602d2e2eced00/1613574292)
Open image viewer
The corona era increased people's loneliness. Photo: Mimmi Nietula / Yle

Many Finns experience loneliness. A study says that 20 percent of people experience strong loneliness. The loneliness experienced by children and young people in particular increased a lot during the corona era. This happened because people had to avoid meeting other people.
Professor Niina Junttila researches loneliness. Junttila is worried that for many Finns the feeling of loneliness has not eased, even though corona restrictions have been removed.
The reason may be that people have got used to avoiding gatherings and other people.
## Sälen security meeting
![Pekka Haavisto.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5119,h_2879,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-105676063baba404872e/1673181784)
Open image viewer
Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto spoke at the Sälen security conference in Sweden. Photo: Lehtikuva
The traditional Sälen security conference has begun in Sweden. This year the most important topic of the meeting is Sweden's and Finland's NATO membership.

Participants include, for example, the Swedish Prime Minister, the Secretary General of NATO and Finland's Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto. Foreign Minister Haavisto said at the meeting that Finland and Sweden will join NATO together. Finland does not want to join NATO without Sweden.
Turkey and Hungary have not yet approved Finland's and Sweden's NATO membership.
## Eating vegetables

![Vegetable section of a grocery store, general view, 28.12.2016.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5472,h_3076,x_0,y_282/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/17-722145864b51f49dc5/1482995051)
Open image viewer
Rising food prices can increase inequality. Photo: Ilkka Klemola / Yle

The rise in food prices affects Finns' food choices. For example, in S-Group shops the share of vegetables, fruit and root vegetables in people's shopping has decreased since last August. The reason may be rising prices.
At the end of last year the share of vegetables, fruit and root vegetables in purchases was 15 percent. Previously the share was 17 percent.
Professor of nutrition science Maijaliisa Erkkola is worried that inequality may increase if some people have to save on eating vegetables.
## The weather
![Monday's weather map.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-12687521)
Open image viewer
In the west and north there is drifting snow.

On Monday snow falls in almost the whole of Finland. In the west and north the snow may drift heavily. In the south and west the temperature is between -1 and -5 degrees. In the north and east the temperature is between -8 and -12 degrees.
